Title: Intra-host diversity of drug-resistant cytomegalovirus: A case report of cytomegalovirus infection after allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation.
Aim.of.study: Case report of resistant CMV in HSCT
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 14 days post transplant, CMV reactivated. BK virus also detected, treated with CDV. CMV kept rising. Changed to GCV, initial decrease in VL, but reactivated at day 60. GCV continued. CMV gastritis detected and CMV VL increased. Changed to FOS. CMV resolved but symptoms of GVHD so increased immunosuppression, leading to CMV reactivation, GCV restarted, immunosuppression reduced, VL decreased. CMV reactivation day 165, CMV colitis and CMV pneumonia. VL did not decrease despite GCV, so changed to FOS and no immunosuppressants. Resistance detected day 199 and 224. Started on GCV and leflunomide in addition to FOS. Psychological symptoms at day 260, CMV detected in CSF, CMV meningoencephalitis. L595W/F412L mutations detected in CSF. Patient passed away day 279 due to CMV infection and multiple organ failure

Clinical.comments.Patients: Paediatric AML, HSCT D-/R+. CMV reactivated at 19 days post transplant. Had four more recurrent CMV infections over 19.4 months. GVHD. H600L/T700A detected 1237 and 1241 days post transplant after 50 days FOS. Changed to CDV, then added GCV. T700A returned to WT when M460V/E756G detected at 1272, 1297, 1332, 1363, 1393 days post transplant.Changed to GCV and FOS at 1332 days post transplant. Received a total of 61 days GCV, 50 days FOS throughout course of infection. Developed CMV GI, retinitis, pneumonia. Treated resistance with CDV, CMV IVIG. Passed away from CMV pneumonia. Patient described in Park 2022 (Covidence 7733) and Choi 2014 (Covidence 155)

Clinical.comments.Patients: Paediatric AML, HSCT D-/R+. CMV reactivated at 19 days post transplant. Had four more recurrent CMV infections over 19.4 months. GVHD. H600L/T700A detected 1237 and 1241 days post transplant after 50 days FOS. Changed to CDV, then added GCV. T700A returned to WT when M460V/E756G detected at 1272, 1297, 1332, 1363, 1393 days post transplant.Changed to GCV and FOS at 1332 days post transplant. Received a total of 61 days GCV, 50 days FOS throughout course of infection. Developed CMV GI, retinitis, pneumonia. Treated resistance with CDV, CMV IVIG. Passed away from CMV pneumonia. Patient described in Park 2022 (Covidence 7733) and Choi 2014 (Covidence 155)

Title: Improved detection of emerging drug-resistant mutant cytomegalovirus subpopulations by deep sequencing.
Aim.of.study: Case study assessing deep sequencing for identifying CMV resistance
Study.investigates: Prevalence of resistance in patients; Phenotypic testing to determine resistance
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: 454 pyrosequencing, Sanger. UL97 codons 375-650 and UL54 300-1000.
Clinical.comments.Patients: Adult CLL, unsuccessful SCT. VGCV pre-emptive therapy. Five weeks later CMV detected. Continuing CMV viral load despite VGCV, C607Y detected. Changed to FOS and CMV IVIG for possible CMV pneumonia. Bronchoscopy positive for pneymocystis (CMV negative). After 6 weeks FOS, reduced dose and then changed to VGCV. Developed CMV pneumonia, C607Y/A594V/L773V/A809V/Q578L detected, changed to high-dose GCV alongside CDV. 2 weeks later A594V disappeared and V715M detected low level. Pneumonia stabilised and improved, discharged with VGCV. CMV viral load rose quickly, C607Y/A594V/L773V/A809V/DEL981-982/N408D/C539G/A834P/P522S/D413N detected, then C607Y/A594V/DEL981-982/C539G/A809V/P522S/N408D/D413N detected 3 weeks later. CLL relapsed and ongoing CMV infection excluded for further chemotherapy or transplantation. Patient passed away.

Title: How evolution of mutations conferring drug resistance affects viral dynamics and clinical outcomes of cytomegalovirus-infected hematopoietic cell transplant recipients.
Aim.of.study: Identify mutations causing resistance and characterise novel mutations
Study.investigates: Prevalence of resistance in patients; Phenotypic testing to determine resistance
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger, AD169
Clinical.comments.Patients: CMV reactivation 56 days post transplant. Treated with FOS then GCV and CMV IVIG. CMV resolved and continued GCV prophylaxis. CMV reactivated and developed CMV gastritis and colitis. Treated with GCV and CMV IVIG, CMV persisted. M460V/C592G detected in blood, 139 days post transplant. Changed to FOS. CMV VL fluctuations for several months. CDV administered for adenovirus infection and reduced FOS during this time. Patient developed RSV pneumonitis, treated with ribavirin and RSV IVIG. CMV reactivated while on low dose FOS then A594V/T838A detected in respiratory isolate. Developed CMV colitis. 650 days post transplant patient developed colonic pneumatosis and passed away from respiratory and renal failure. Post mortem showed CMV and pneumocystis carinii in BAL and L802M mutations.

Title: How evolution of mutations conferring drug resistance affects viral dynamics and clinical outcomes of cytomegalovirus-infected hematopoietic cell transplant recipients.
Aim.of.study: Identify mutations causing resistance and characterise novel mutations
Study.investigates: Prevalence of resistance in patients; Phenotypic testing to determine resistance
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger, AD169
Clinical.comments.Patients: Developed severe disseminated CMV with pneumonitis, esophagitis, colitis and cerebrates. Treated with GCV but developed GCV neutropenia. 7 years post transplant, patient developed CMV retinitis, treated with GCV/FOS/CMV IVIG then GCV. Recurring CMV pneumonitis, colitis and retinitis. V812L mutation detected in blood, then C592G mutation detected in gastric isolate. D588N mutation detected. Patient received second and third HSCT, continued CMV reactivations. Patient passed away due to aspergillosis and post mortem shows BAL CMV and aspergillus.

Title: Emergence of letermovir resistance in solid organ transplant recipients with ganciclovir resistant cytomegalovirus infection: A case series and review of the literature.
Aim.of.study: Case series of GCV resistance treated with LET in KTR
Genes.targeted: UL51; UL54; UL56; UL89; UL97; Other: Merlin
Clinical.comments.Patients: GCV prophylaxis, asymptomatic CMV, resistance detected. GCV dose increased and immunosuppression reduced, but did not control CMV and CMV retinitis and GI disease. FOS and intravitreal FOS resolved CMV. LET prophylaxis and CMV IVIG. Patient developed EBV and immunosuppressants were reduced. Insufficient LET dose led to CMV VL increased so FOS started. FOS resolved CMV and LET restarted but CMV VL increased again. LET resistance detected. FOS restarted. Patient passed away due to EBV disease

Title: Emergence of letermovir resistance in solid organ transplant recipients with ganciclovir resistant cytomegalovirus infection: A case series and review of the literature.
Aim.of.study: Case series of GCV resistance treated with LET in KTR
Genes.targeted: UL51; UL54; UL56; UL89; UL97; Other: Merlin
Clinical.comments.Patients: VGCV prophylaxis. CMV reactivation, VGCV dose increased. CMV CTL's also given, but VL increased and suspicion of CMV colitis. Patient refused FOS so GCV continued. VL increased. Symptomatic CMV patient agreed to FOS and immunosuppression reduced.CMV resolved. LET prophylaxis started, some low level CMV detected. Rejection treated with high-dose steroids, symptomatic CMV returned. LET/GCV resistance, so LET replaced with FOS, CMV IVIG and reduced immunosuppression. CMV resolved and FOS discontinued. Patient immune system improved to control CMV

Title: Artesunate as a potent antiviral agent in a patient with late drug-resistant cytomegalovirus infection after hematopoietic stem cell transplantation.
Aim.of.study: Case report of artesunate to treat drug resistant CMV
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: UL97 nucleotides 1207 to 1979 and UL54 nucleotides 900 to 3000 only.
Clinical.comments.Patients: CMV reactivation 15 days post transplantation. Treated with FOS, initial CMV VL decrease. Reactivation day 119 despite continuous FOS. Patient received second SCT. CMV persisted despite GCV, CDV and CMV IVIG. Changed to artesunate, CMV VL reduced and did not rebound for 76 days after artesunate stopped. Patient received 3rd SCT and had another CMV reactivation, artesunate reduced CMV VL, but patient developed CMV retinitis. Added intravitreal GCV injections which resolved CMV retinitis. No further reactivations.

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97

Treatment was interrupted after 4 weeks with negative viraemia and no symptoms. Soon CMV recurred, treated with 2 weeks of GCV. After stopping GCV again, CMV detected. Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: VGCV prophylaxis, developed CMV infection, VGCV dose increased. Did not respond, VL increased, changed to IV GCV. Initial VL increase, but later reduced, then switched back to VGCV. Leukopenia, thrombocytopenia and diarrhoea, VL increased, back to IV GCV. No resistance detected. Switched to FOS, reduced VL, then switched back to VGCV. CMV ileitis, GCV and CMV IVIG, did not respond, switched to FOS, GCV resistance detected. FOS caused increased creatinine and nephrotoxicity so disruptions in FOS treatment, leading to spiked in CMV VL. LET started, acute diarrhoea, CMV reduced and disease resolved. Supply issues caused spikes in VL, but continual LET led to CMV clearance without further reactivations

Title: Resistance to combined ganciclovir and foscarnet therapy in a liver transplant recipient with possible dual-strain cytomegalovirus coinfection.
Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV resistance in liver transplant recipient
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: AD169
Clinical.comments.Patients: 30 days post transplant CMV reactivation. Treated with GCV and reduced immunosuppression and then VGCV for 49 days. VGCV reduced to prophylaxis dose for 30 days. 114 days post transplant CMV reactivated, treated with VGCV then GCV. No impact on CMV VL, so FOS was added to GCV for 33 days and CMV reduced but not cleared. CMV rose again 202 days post transplant, treated with GCV and then GCV/FOS for 12 days. Then changed to VGCV and CMV became asymptomatic. Patient passed away 20 months post transplant due to complications despite asymptomatic CMV disease. UL54 mutations only detected in first reactivation and UL97 mutations detected in second reactivation

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: UL97 RFLP and UL54 sequencing. Reference sequence AD169 (accession no. X17403).
Clinical.comments.Patients: SCID, CMV respiratory illness 25 days of age, GCV, SCT at 8 weeks of age with GCV throughout. CMV would not resolve so changed to FOS, again would not resolve so back to GCV but neutropenia so stopped for 20 days then recommenced with CMV IVIG when patient developed CMV colitis. CMV reduced but persisted, no resistance detected. Changed to FOS for 3 weeks then back to GCV for 2 years where CMV colitis resolved and CMV intermittently detected, but patient alive and no further CMV disease. Retrospective testing identified UL97 mutation 1 month prior to original testing and intermittent WT/R for 1 year and UL54 mutation appeared after UL97 disappeared, 1 year after FOS treatment stopped.

Title: Cytomegalovirus ventriculoencephalitis in a peripheral blood stem cell transplant recipient.

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Severe GVHD day 79 post transplant, treated with high-dose steroids, CMV reactivated treated with GCV or FOS over 3 months. CMV VL reduced, but reactivated after stopping treatment. Neurological symptoms, increased FOS, CMV detected in CSF. GCV added to FOS. Patient deceased. Retrospective testing showed A885T and S897L detected in CSF, V787A only detected in blood.

Title: Emergence and compartmentalization of fatal multi-drug-resistant cytomegalovirus infection in a patient with autosomal-recessive severe combined immune deficiency.
Aim.of.study: Case report of SCID patient with multi drug resistant CMV
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: UL144
Clinical.comments.Patients: SCID. Fullterm uncomplicated pregnancy. 4 weeks of age, failure to thrive and anemia. Presented for care at 13 weeks old. CSF grew acinetobacter baumanii. Diagnosed with SCID. Alveolar disease, CMV deteted in BAL. Repeat CMV testing on CSF found detected but below limit result. CMV retinitis. Started on GCV and IVIG with good response. Clinically improved over 6 weeks, GCV dose decreased, but day 58, viral load increased again. Day 65 GCV increased. CMV continued to increase, FOS started day 74. VL reduced in one week. M460V/M460I/A594V detected day 86. HSCT performed dat 115, GCV discontinued day 117 due to resistance detection and potential GCV-myelosuppression. Neurologic status decreased and GCV restarted alongside CDV for presumed CMV encephalitis. L595S detected in blood and M460I/M460V in urine at day 136. CSF WT. Neurologic status improved, and VL reduced. No evidence of marrow engraftment. Day 210, respiratory distress, and respiratory failure on day 212. Multiorgan failure 219. L595S/K513N/T700A detected day 219. CMV pneumonitis. Despite GCV, FOS, CDV, passed away day 228.

Title: Multidrug-resistant cytomegalovirus infection in a pediatric stem cell transplantation patient.
Aim.of.study: Case study of multi drug resistance in paediatric SCT
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger, AD169 (GenBank X17403)
Clinical.comments.Patients: 4 month old, failure to thrive, presumed immunodeficiency, CMV detected in blood. Treated with GCV. MHC class II deficiency diagnosed. 4 weeks later GCV dose frequency reduced, but CMV VL increased and regular dosing resumed. VL continued to increase, switched to FOS and CMV IVIG. M460V detected in nasopharangeal aspirate (NPA), CSF and blood. Patient deteriorated, despite treatment and developed CMV encephalitis. HSCT performed D+/R+. Possible central CMV infection, CDV added to FOS. M460V/DEL981-982 detected in blood and NPA at 1 day post transplant. 13 days post transplant respiratory symptoms exacerbated, CDV stopped due to cytopenia and increased viral load. 19 days post transplant M460V had reverted to WT, but DEL981-982 still detected. Clinical deterioration of respiratory and liver function and uncontrollable sepsis, started on palliative care. DEL981-982 detected in blood NPA and urine up to 33 days post transplant. Patient passed away 36 days post transplant with encephalitis, respiratory and cardiac arrest.

Title: Emergence of Letermovir-resistant HCMV UL56 mutant during rescue treatment in a liver transplant recipient with ganciclovir-resistant infection HCMV: a case report.
Aim.of.study: Case report of LET resistance in liver transplant recipient
Genes.targeted: UL51; UL54; UL56; UL89; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 5 weeks post transplant CMV detected, VGCV started. 11 weeks VL increased, changed to GCV increased dose but had to be reduced due to myelotoxicity. CMV VL persisted after 13 weeks of treatment then increased. GCV Resistance detected, changed to FOS but electrolyte side-effects, so discontinued and CMV VL increased further. GCV restarted but no effect on VL and worsening anaemia and thrombocytopenia so also stopped. 20 weeks resduced immunosuppressants, but had to be increased again due to neurological complications. CMV pneumonitis and MRSA at week 21. GCV reintroduced with CMV IVIG. Same mutation detected. Week 30 VL increased. 32 weeks changed to LET only. VL decreased after 5 weeks, but increased after 7 and 8 weeks. LET resistance detected and retrospective testing showed mutation at 5 weeks post LET. Changed to CDV, VL increased, no CDV resistance detected. Patient passed away due to CMV complications

Title: Pyrosequencing allows the detection of emergent ganciclovir resistance mutations after HCMV infection.
Aim.of.study: Demonstrate utility of pyrosequencing for monitoring CMV resistance
Genes.targeted: UL97; Other: RFLP, Sanger and pyrosequencing, UL97 codons 439 to 696 only.
Clinical.comments.Patients: GCV started 5 days old, VL reduced. M460V/A594G detected in CSF at 10 days old. Agranulocytosis, despite reduced GCV dose, so stopped after 19 days. Title: Multiple ganciclovir-resistant strains in a newborn with symptomatic congenital human cytomegalovirus infection.
Aim.of.study: GCV resistance in cCMV
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger
Clinical.comments.Patients: First pregnancy, primary CMV infection. Congenital CMV infection, born 33 weeks by cesarian section. Presented with intrauterine growth retardation, microcefalia, intracerebra calcifications,slightventriculomegaly, neuromotor disabilities, hepatosplenomegaly, hepatitis, thrombocytopenia and petechiae. CMV detected in blood 1 day old. Treated with GCV from 2 days old, but discontinued at day 13 due to neutropenia. Progressive clinical deterioration at day 37, VGCV started. No clinical improvement and VL persisted. 25 days old bilateral transmission delay to audiometry. 75 days of unsuccessful VGCV treatment (day 112) started on GCV for one week. No improvement. High-level CMV VL, respiratory distress and thrombocytopenia. Day 113 M460V/C592G/A594V detected in blood. Started on FOS at day 127, significant improvement and reduced VL. FOS discontinued day 173 (47 days treatment). One month later CMV still detected. Patient passed away at 8 months of age from pulmonary complications.

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger

Title: Ganciclovir-resistant cytomegalovirus (CMV) retinitis in a patient with wild-type CMV in her plasma.
Aim.of.study: Case report of GCV resistant retinitis with WT in blood
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Presented with neurological symptoms and CMV detected in blood and CSF. Started on GCV. No visual symptoms, but lesions in eyes. FOS shortage, so GCV injections. CMV detected in both eyes. After 11 days with no improvement changed to brincidofovir. Intestinal side effects caused changing back to GCV after 10 days and improvement in VL after 2 weeks. Intravitreal injections changed to FOS, but condition worsened. New resistance detected in eye. FOS injections improved condition with no further relapses 9 months post presentation.

Title: Virologic characterization of multidrug-resistant cytomegalovirus infection in 2 transplant recipients treated with maribavir.

Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: Lung, heart

Clinical.comments.Patients: Heart, 6 months VGCV prophylaxis. 9 months post transplant, CMV reactivation, treated with GCV and CMV resolved after 7 weeks and GCV stopped. CMV reactivated and restarted on GCV and immunosuppression reduced but developed rejection so increased immunosuppression. CMV resistance detected, switched to FOS/GCV/CMV IVIG. Isolate cloned into Ecoli and sequenced to find variant frequency, H411Y 64%, H411N 7% and T409M 29%. No mutations found in UL27 despite suspected MBV resistance.

Title: Dynamics of cytomegalovirus populations harbouring mutations in genes UL54 and UL97 in a haematopoietic stem cell transplant recipient.

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger and pyrosequencing
Clinical.comments.Patients: 10 months prior to transplant primary CMV infection resulting in prolonged neutropenia. 10 days post transplant CMV reactivated, started on FOS. VL reduced and changed to VGCV after 19 days then GCV. CMV VL reduced further then maintenance dose GCV. VL increased, FOS added. CMV VL reduced, GCV stopped. VL relapsed, GCV restarted, CMV persisted. FOS changed to brincidofovir day 185, CMV persisted, side-effects so stopped after 36 days. A594V/A834P/Q578H detected day 222. Resistance testing performed retrospectively to investigate kinetics

Title: Successful outcome of ganciclovir-resistant cytomegalovirus infection in organ transplant recipients after conversion to mTOR inhibitors.
Aim.of.study: Case series of GCV resistant infections resolved after mTOR immunosuppressive regimen
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: Heart, kidney
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Heart, 2 weeks post transplant, rejection, increased immunosuppression. 1 week later CMV detected, treated with VGCV, CMV resolved, continued VGCV for 2 months. One month after finishing, CMV reactivated, GCV, VL increased. A594V detected, changed to FOS, side-effects so discontinued after 2 weeks. CMV VL increased significantly within 4 days, immunosuppression changed to everolimus. CMV resolved without antivirals and side effects resolved. No further reactivations

Title: Successful outcome of ganciclovir-resistant cytomegalovirus infection in organ transplant recipients after conversion to mTOR inhibitors.
Aim.of.study: Case series of GCV resistant infections resolved after mTOR immunosuppressive regimen
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: Heart, kidney
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Kidney, 2 months post transplant, bacteraemic pyelonephritis and CMV. Treated with VGCV, CMV resolved, continued VGCV. Recurrent bacteraemic pyelonephritis required bilateral nephrectomy, one week later CMV reactivated. Changed to GCV, A595S detected, stopped GCV and changed to sirolimus immunosuppressive regimen. CMV resolved without antiviral therapy. No further reactivations

Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV resistance in HIV patient
Genes.targeted: UL97; Other: Sanger, AD169
Clinical.comments.Patients: No CMV detected in CSF. CMV detected in biopsy, CMV gastritis. Patient deceased due to lymphoma.

Title: UL54 foscarnet mutation in an hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipient with cytomegalovirus disease.
Aim.of.study: Case report of FOS resistance in HSCT recipient
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: HHV-6 infection treated with FOS, EBV infection which was cleared after 1 dose of rituximab. Developed CMV 8 days after stopping FOS. Successfully treated colitis and CMV became negative

Title: Ganciclovir-resistant cytomegalovirus encephalitis in a bone marrow transplant recipient.
Aim.of.study: Case report of GCV resistance in SCT recipient
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Sanger
Clinical.comments.Patients: GVHD, aspergillus infection. Acyclovir prophylaxis. 66 days post transplant CMV reactivated, IV GCV and CMV IVIG, CMV resolved. IV GCV continued until day 130. Reactivation day 129, changed to FOS, resolved by 150 maintenance dose of FOS.  Neurological symptoms day 166, FOS stopped day 177, no CMV in CSF dat 178, day 182 changed to IV GCV. Patient passed away day 192 due to CMV brain lesions and panlobar bronchopneumonia. Mutations detected in both brain tissue and spinal fluid

Title: Treatment of multidrug-resistant cytomegalovirus retinitis with systemically administered leflunomide.
Aim.of.study: Case report of multi-drug resistance treated with leflunomide in KTR
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: VGCV prophylaxis, 6 months post transplant developed CMV pneumonitis, colitis and retinitis. Increased VGCV dose showed some clinical improvement, but developed leucopenia requiring reduced VGCV and reduced immunosuppression. Varied compliance with VGCV due to side effects, continued VGCV for 14 months. CMV reactivation so increased VGCV dose but patient self-adjusted, so changed to CMV IVIG and GCV. CMV retinitis developed further and resistance detected. Changed to FOS and CMV IVIG, retinitis improved and VL reduced. 5 months on FOS CMV IVIG and retinitis reactivated and further resistance detected. Vitrectomy and GCV implant, but retinitis continued to progress, intraocular FOS which worked on right eye but not left. Resistance detected in vitreous. Patient started on leflunomide, VL reduced but retinitis progressed. Fomivirsen intraocular injections given in left eye and FOS in right eye. Active retinitis in both eyes despite treatment. Continued leflunomide and cataract extraction retinitis resolved. CMV VL reactivated and had slow response to increased leflunomide dose.

Title: Surgical treatment of a foscavir-resistant atypical Cytomegalovirus pneumonia in an allogeneic stem cell transplant recipient.
Aim.of.study: Case study of resistance treated with surgery
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Adult CML, SCT, GVHD. CMV detected 45 days post transplant, treated with GCV/VGCV. CMV resolved 76 days. CMV recurred day 180, treated with VGCV. VL persisted, resistance suspected. M460V detected day 180, CMV colitis day 229. Changed to FOS, CMV VL decreased. Day 200 started respiratory symptoms, low-level CMV despite FOS from day 254 to 310. Day 320 VL increased. Given foscavir. Lung resection performed day 345. Discovered CMV lesions in tissue. V946F detected in blood, V948F/N495 detected in lung. Remained negative for CMV VL from 352 to 7 months after resection.

Title: Letermovir use to treat complex cytomegalovirus reactivations in two heart transplant recipients.
Aim.of.study: Case reports of letermovir use for CMV
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Adult severe idiopathic cariomyopathy, heart transplant D+/R-. VGCV prophylaxis for 4 months. CMV detected, changed to GCV for 2 weeks, then VGCV for 3 weeks. CMV resolved and continued VGCV prophylaxis. CMV rose again, VGCV dose increased. CMV colitis, A594V detected. Changed to LET for 3.5 months. CMV resolved and remained negative.

Title: Persistent Primary Cytomegalovirus Infection After Deceased Donor Kidney Transplant: Ganciclovir Susceptibility of Human Cytomegalovirus With UL97 D605E Mutation: A Case Report.
Aim.of.study: Case report of refractory CMV infection in paediatric KTR
Study.investigates: Prevalence of resistance in patients; Phenotypic testing to determine resistance
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: CMV detected 1 month post transplant, started on GCV. Graft function decreased, so decreased GCV dose. Developed acute rejection 2 months post transplant. CMV VL increased at 5 months and started on CMV IVIG. CMV persisted. Resistance testing and changed to FOS and CMV resolved. FOS then ceased, but patient developed CMV retinitis and FOS nephrotoxicity. Changed back to GCV. CMV resolved and retinitis improved.

Title: Letermovir breakthroughs during the French Named Patient Programme: interest of monitoring blood concentration in clinical practice.
Aim.of.study: NA
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL56; UL89; UL97; Other: Sanger Sequencing and Ion torrent, SRA accession PRJNA593377.
Clinical.comments.Patients: Adult multiple myeloma SCT. Letermovir from day 273 as secondary prophylaxis after CMV successfully controlled by GCV and FOS without any resistance. CMV rebounded after 1 month LET, but no resistance. After 50 days LET, changed to FOS. VL increased 2 weeks later and C325Y detected. Changed to GCV, but CMV continued to reoccur. Retrospective NGS testing found C325Y at 99%.

Title: Brincidofovir Use after Foscarnet Crystal Nephropathy in a Kidney Transplant Recipient with Multiresistant Cytomegalovirus Infection.
Aim.of.study: Case report of multi drug resistance CMV in KTR treated with brincidofovir
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: VGCV prophylaxis for 6 months. 222 days post transplant (1 month after stopping VGCV), CMV reactivated and developed CMV gastritis. Started GCV and reduced immunosuppression. CMV resolved. CMV reactivated 1 week after stopping GCV and relapse of CMV gastritis. Started GCV, no improvement over 2 weeks, resistance detected, started on FOS day 306. CMV resolved and FOS tapered off day 320. CMV reactivated day 329, started on FOS, 6 days later graft failure, FOS nephropathy. CMV reduced FOS stopped. CMV reactivation day 341, high-dose GCV and CMV IVIG started. L595S mutation still detected so started on brincidofovir day 376 for 21 days. Some side effects so stopped, then CMV reactivation, started brincidofovir again for 15 days. CMV gastritis and side-effects. UL54 mutation detected. Restarted FOS, CMV resolved. No further reactivations.

Title: Viral escape and T-cell immunity during ganciclovir treatment of cytomegalovirus infection: case report of a pancreatico-renal transplant recipient.
Aim.of.study: Monitor CD8+ T-cells during CMV infection
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: Pancreas and Kidney
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Adult diabetes, kidney and pancreas D+/R-. Half dose prophylaxis due to renal insufficiency (GCV then VGCV). 10 weeks post transplant while on VGCV, developed CMV posthitis. CMV CTL's and IVIG. CMV resolved and VGCV stopped 34 weeks post transplantation. 13 months post transplant CMV reoccurred with CMV colitis. 10 days GCV, with clinical improvement. 6 weeks later symptomatic, but low VL. High-dose GCV for 2 weeks with clinical improvement, but colitis persisted. Resistance detected. Retrospective testing identified mutations from 13 months post transplant. Did not want to change to potentially nephrotoxic antiviral treatment, so removed GCV and treated with IVIG and CTLs. 20 months post transplantation colitis resolved. Alive

CMV IVIG added. FOS side-effects , but CMV reduced. Started on LET prophylaxis. Some fluctuations of CMV VL on LET, but no CMV disease. After 11 weeks of LT, CMV reactivated, resistance detected. Changed back to FOS and CMV reduced. Two more reactivations controlled with FOS, C325Y mutation persisted 20 weeks after stopping LET so could not change back to LET.

Title: Case Report: Management of a Multidrug-Resistant CMV-Strain in a Renal Transplant Recipient by High-Dose CMV-Specific Immunoglobulins, Modulation in Immunosuppression, and Induction of CMV-Specific Cellular Immunity
Aim.of.study: Case report of multi drug resistance in KTR
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 5th kidney transplant, VGCV prophylaxis for 3 months. One week after stopping VGCV, CMV reactivated, restarted VGCV at therapeutic dosage. CMV VL increased, changed to GCV at 21 weeks post transplant. Developed leukopenia and thrombopenia. Started CMV IVIG and reduced immunosuppression. CMV VL further increased. 23 weeks post transplant resistance detected. GCV stopped, changed immunosuppression, administered high-dose CMV IVIG. CMV VL further increased, but then decreased a week later. Developed rejection, but CMV resolved. No further reactivations.

Title: Successful Treatment with Letermovir in a Heart Transplant Recipient with UL97 Mutation Ganciclovir-Resistant Cytomegalovirus Colitis and Viremia.
Aim.of.study: Case report of GCV resistant CMV in HTR treated with LET
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Acyclovir prophylaxis, 7 weeks post transplant CMV reactivated, changed to VGCV for 6 months. Day 858 developed CMV colitis, treated with GCV, improved and changed to VGCV. Developed bacterial pneumonia, had neutropenia so reduced VGCV dose. CMV reactivated 1402 days post transplant, VGCV dose increased. Reactivated again 2088 days post transplant and VL increasing despite VGCV. Changed to GCV, CMV IVIG and reduced immunosuppressants. CMV VL increased, resistance detected. Unable to administer FOS or CDV due to kidney disease, so started on LET. CMV resolved within 30 days and stopped LET. No further reactivations.

Title: Letermovir as Salvage Therapy for Cytomegalovirus Infection in Transplant Recipients.
Aim.of.study: Describe the efficacy of LET to treat resistant and refractory CMV infections in transplant recipients
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Stem Cell Transplant; Other: Lung
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL56; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Lung, VGCV prophylaxis for 6.5 months. CMV reactivated 1 week after stopping VGCV, VGCV increased then changed to GCV. Resistance detected. Changed to FOS, CMV resolved within 3 weeks, FOS stopped. VL increased 2 weeks later, immunosuppressants reduced, FOS restarted but only partial response so LET added. CMV resolved after 2 weeks, FOS discontinued after 3 weeks, LET discontinued after 8 weeks. No further reactivations.

Title: Letermovir as Salvage Therapy for Cytomegalovirus Infection in Transplant Recipients.
Aim.of.study: Describe the efficacy of LET to treat resistant and refractory CMV infections in transplant recipients
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Stem Cell Transplant; Other: Lung
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL56; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: HSCT, 6 months post transplant had 3 episodes of CMV treated with GCV then VGCV. VGCV prophylaxis continued after third reactivation. 8 months post transplant CMV VL increased, VGCV changed to GCV, CMV persisted after 6 weeks GCV so dose increased. Resistance detected but VL reduced after 2 months GCV. VL increased, GCV restarted, no response, changed to FOS, VL further increased after 6 weeks. Developed CMV colitis and CMV pneumonitis. Additional resistance detected. LET added to FOS, VL decreased after 1 months, but developed sepsis and FOS associated kidney injury. Decision made to discontinue further treatment and patient passed away.

Title: Immune restoration therapy for multidrug-resistant CMV disease in an allogenic stem cell transplant recipient
Aim.of.study: Case report of multi drug resistant CMV in SCT recipient
Study.investigates: Prevalence of resistance in patients; Phenotypic testing to determine resistance
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97; Other: Ion torrent
Clinical.comments.Patients: 23 days post transplant CMV detected and started on GCV. Initial VL reduction but then increased. FOS added to GCV. Resistance detected 127 days post transplant. 6 months post transplant GVHD. GCV treatment unsuccessful, CMV IVIG added, no change. CMV colitis day 370. First-line antivirals ceased and adjustments to immunosuppressants to boost T-cell responses and artesunate administered for 7 months. CMV colitis resolved and VL reduced. Relapse of VL day 450. More resistance detected. GCV restarted and CMV resolved. No further reactivations

Title: Analysis of Novel Drug-Resistant Human Cytomegalovirus DNA Polymerase Mutations Reveals the Role of a DNA-Binding Loop in Phosphonoformic Acid Resistance
Aim.of.study: Characterisation of novel UL54 mutations found in paediatric HSCT recipient
Study.investigates: Prevalence of resistance in patients; Phenotypic testing to determine resistance
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: Paediatric AML, HSCT D-/R+. CMV reactivated at 19 days post transplant. Had four more recurrent CMV infections over 19.4 months. GVHD. H600L/T700A detected 1237 and 1241 days post transplant after 50 days FOS. Changed to CDV, then added GCV. T700A returned to WT when M460V/E756G detected at 1272, 1297, 1332, 1363, 1393 days post transplant.Changed to GCV and FOS at 1332 days post transplant. Received a total of 61 days GCV, 50 days FOS throughout course of infection. Developed CMV GI, retinitis, pneumonia. Treated resistance with CDV, CMV IVIG. Passed away from CMV pneumonia. Patient described in Park 2022 (Covidence 7733) and Choi 2014 (Covidence 155)

Title: Letermovir salvage therapy in the management of a case of cytomegalovirus ventriculitis complicated by drug resistance
Aim.of.study: Case study of Letermovir to treat multi drug resistance in HIV patient.
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL56; UL97; Other: Sanger, AD169
Clinical.comments.Patients: Adult HIV-AIDS. CMV detected in CSF and blood. CMV ventriculitis. Started on GCV for 4 weeks then VGCV. 6 months later worsening cognition, suboptimal drug adherance. CMV remained undetected in blood, but detected in CSF with resistance. Changed to FOS, but CMV remained in CSF. Changed to LET with VL reduced 100-fold over 4 weeks. 2 months later admitted to ICU for hospital acquired pneumonia and CMV VL increased in CSF. Patient passed away shortly thereafter.

Title: Real-life experience in two cases of secondary prophylaxis with letermovir for CMV infection in solid organ transplantation
Aim.of.study: Two case reported of secondary prophylaxis with LET
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: Lung, Liver
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL56; UL97; Other: UL97 270-670, UL54 300-1000 and UL56 180-395. Sanger sequencing. TB40 MF871618.1 reference. MRA for analysis.
Clinical.comments.Patients: VGCV prophylaxis 4.5 months, but discontinued due to neutropenia. 1 year later developed CMV GI disease, treated with VGCV but again discontinued. Title: Refractory anti-viral resistant CMV retinitis in an immunological nonresponder person living with HIV
Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV retinitis and resistance in HIV patient
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 43yo with disseminated mycobacterium avium and CMV retinitis and possible CMV colitis. Treated with GCV for 7 weeks, retinitis slowly healed. Changed to VGCV for 7 weeks. CMV VL increased, VGCV dose increased, resistance detected and changed to FOS. VL decreased and no retinitis. 14 weeks later CMV and retinitis rebounded. A809V detected. Changed to CDV, CMV IVIG, and intravitreal GCV. VL continued to increase and retinitis worsened. P522S detected, high-dose GCV, CDV and IVIG. CMV VL decreased and retinitis improved. 1 month later VL resolved changed to VGCV, CDV (less frequent) and IVIG (less frequent). Developed treatment induced pancytopenia, requiring stopping of VGCV. CMV rebounded 2 weeks later, VGCV and CDV restarted. VL controlled for 10 weeks. VGCV discontinued, then 1 week later VL increased. No resistance detected, so restarted VGCV for 3 weeks. Changed to LET. Relapse of retinitis, even though CMV negative in blood. 3 weeks of VGCV resolved retinitis then VGCV LET and IVIC continued to control CMV

Title: Efficacy of ganciclovir versus foscarnet in ganciclovir-resistant cytomegalovirus retinitis: A case report

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: CMV retinitis successfully treated with GCV. 3 years later, developed CMV colitis. Resistance detected, started on FOS and CMV resolved. 3 months later, retinitis recurred. Intravitreal GCV administered, but no improvement, so intravitreal FOS given. Retinitis progressed so switched back to intravitreal GCV. Resolved.

Aim.of.study: Case report of MBV in patient with renal impairment
Genes.targeted: UL97

Title: Emergence of maribavir resistance after CMV treatment in hematopoietic stem cell transplant recipient.
Aim.of.study: Case report of MBV resistance
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: AML underwent AlloHCT, D+/R-, received LET prophylaxis until day 100 post transplant. CMV detected 1813 IU/mL at day 158, treated with FOS for 4 weeks. Day 212 developed CMV colitis, resistance ND. Treated with FOS, followed by MBV for 6 weeks, symptoms and DNAemia resolved. Day 273 CMV 1573 IU/mL, restarted on MBV, peaked at 2830 IU/mL on day 316 and colitis recurred. MBV resistance detected. Treated with FOS, followed by VGCV, symptoms and DNAemia resolved. Secondary prophylaxis with LET.

Title: Use of Maribavir for Multidrug Resistant Cytomegaloviremia in a Pediatric Oncology Patient.
Aim.of.study: Case report of multi drug resistant CMV in paediatric oncology patient
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 4yo ALL, developed CMV >1000000 copies/mL, alongside HHV6. Started of GCV and then added IVIG after 6 days. Changed to VGCV. CMV VL increased, restarted on VGCV then GCV. CMV VL increased again so changed to FOS. No resistance detected on day 60 of therapy. CMV improved and changed to GCV. Changed from GCV to CDV. CMV persisted so changed to FOS. UL54 mutation detected day 227 of treatment. Changed to CDV and CMV IVIG,  CMV persisted, changed to MBV. CMV increased, UL97 mutation detected 527 days of treatment. Changed back to VGCV. Alive

Title: Cytomegalovirus Retinitis in a Hematopoietic Stem Cell Transplant Recipient During Maribavir Pre-emptive Therapy
Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV retinitis in HSCT recipient
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 52yo CMV detected 2 weeks post transplant, despite being on LET prophylaxis. Switched to VGCV. CMV VL increased, changed to GCV. 4 weeks later CMV still detected, but no resistance detected. Changed to MBV. One month later CMV VL decreased, but then increased. Changed to FOS. Resistance testing performed. CMV retinitis. No resistance detected in vitreal fluid, but resistance detected in plasma. Intravitreal GCV and IV FOS. Then changed to VGCV. CMV and retinitis resolved.

Title: CMV Viremia and Colitis in Simultaneous Pancreas-Kidney Transplantation
Aim.of.study: Case report of difficult to treat CMV infection
Participant.population.clinical.descript: Solid Organ Transplant; Other: kidney and pancreas
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 51yo diabetes, kidney disease, von hippel Lindau syndrome. D+/R-, VGCV prophylaxis. CMV developed day 120 post transplantation. VGCV increased, but CMV VL increased day 150. UL97 resistance mutation detected (not described). Changed to MBV, CMV responded but then rebounded day 180. Developed CMV colitis day 200. Changed to GCV and symptoms resolved. Increased dose of GCV and VL reduced. Day 220 VL increased. Other mutations detected. Changed to FOS, VL reduced, transitioned to LET. CMV became undetected.

Title: Use of Letermovir as Secondary Prophylaxis in Cytomegalovirus Resistant Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients
Aim.of.study: Describe experience with LET as secondary prophylaxis in paediatric heart transplant recipients
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 17yo hypertrophic restrictive cardiomyopathy, VGCV and GCV prophylaxis. CMV detected 34 days post transplant. Treated with GCV, no resistance detected. CMV increased and resistance detected, changed to FOS, CMV VL reduced. After 4 weeks, changed to LET. Continued LET for 4 years, no relapse, alive

Title: Use of Letermovir as Secondary Prophylaxis in Cytomegalovirus Resistant Pediatric Heart Transplant Recipients
Aim.of.study: Describe experience with LET as secondary prophylaxis in paediatric heart transplant recipients
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 13yo cardiomyopathy, VGCV and GCV prophylaxis. CMV detected 20 days post transplant. Transitioned to treatment dose VGCV, CMV VL persisted so changed to IV GCV then resistance detected so changed to FOS and IVIG. CMV resolved and changed to LET. Alive

Title: Letermovir-inclusive combination therapy for a refractory and resistant infection by cytomegalovirus with UL54 mutation following a hematopoietic stem cell transplant for MHC class II deficiency
Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV resistance in paediatric HSCT recipient.
Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 3month old respiratory failure due to CMV and PCP. MHC class II deficiency requiring HSCT. PCP resolved, but CMV persisted. Treated with GCV. CMV persisted, treated with FOS. CMV resolved 4 weeks later and FOS continued. CNS symptoms developed, CMV and HHV6 negative in CSF. CMV VL returned despite FOS. FOS increased but failed to reduce VL. Resistance testing performed. FOS CDV leflunomide and artesunate started. Transplant performed. 2 weeks later, changed to GCV. CDV weekly for 2 weeks then biweekly, leflunomide and art esunate continued. CMV VL continued to rise. UL54 mutation results. Letermovir added to GCV, leflunomide and artsunate. CMV resolved. Possibly developed drug-induced lung injury and passed away 5 months post transplant.

Title: Reversion of Val(ganciclovir)-Resistance Associated Mutation in Two SOT Patients with Mismatch Serostatus for CMV (D+/R-)

Genes.targeted: UL54; UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 30yo Danon disease, heart, VGCV prophylaxis then FOS treatment. Resistance detected 9 months post transplant VL 123750 copies/mL and CMV colitis. Changed to MBV, CMV resolved, changed to LET and VGCV. 1.5 years later stopped LET and no further relapses.

Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV resistance in KTR and LET treatment.
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 59yo chronic kidney disease. VGCV prophylaxis for 3 months post transplant. 4 months post developed CMV 350000 IU/mL. Treated with GCV adjusted to renal function. Clinical improvement, changed to VGCV. 2 months later, symptomatic CMV, restarted GCV. Resistance detected. CMV GI disease. Changed to FOS and CMV IVIG. VL reduced but developed septic shock. FOS changed to LET. Discharged with LET and VGCV. CMV rebounded, started FOS and IVIG. Resolved, changed back to LET and VGCV. Antivirals stopped 3 months later due to no CMV. Did not rebound. Alive.

Title: Pharmacokinetic analysis driven letermovir dosing in pediatric hematopoietic cell transplantation patients with resistant CMV disease.
Aim.of.study: Case report of off-label LET for secondary prophylaxis in Paediatric HSCT recipient with GCV resistant CMV with CMV retinitis
Genes.targeted: UL97
Clinical.comments.Patients: 1yo, D-/R+. CMV reactivated 17 days post transplant. Treated with FOS then switch to GCV. CMV resolved but relapsed day 61, adjusted immunosuppression. Changed back to FOS day 101 until 140 VGCV because second HSCT on day 226 (D+/R+). 34 days post second transplant, CMV VL increased and suspicion of GCV resistance. Developed CMV bilateral retinitis. A594V mutation detected. CMV T-cells on day 47 with continuing FOS> Retinitis resolved and CMV VL reduced. Leukemia relapsed and GVHD developed. CMV worsened, FOS continued until day 257. Changed to LET off-label. Passed away day 336 due to refractory disease.

Title: Revealing the Unseen: Next-Generation Sequencing for Early Detection of Drug-Resistant Cytomegalovirus Variants Upon Letermovir Prophylaxis Failure
Aim.of.study: Case report of CMV resistance during LET prophylaxis
Genes.targeted: UL56; UL97; Other: Illumina and Sanger, reference NC_006273.
Clinical.comments.Patients: 63yo myeloproliferative neoplasm/primary myelofibrosis. D-/R+. LET prophylaxis. CMV reactivated 18 days post transplant. Developed CMV pneumonitis, changed to GCV. C325R detected day 52 (2 weeks before Sanger). C325R became dominant strain by day 67. C325R also found in BAL. CMV VL reduced, changed to VGCV after 3 weeks. Continued decrease. GVHD emerged, causing increased immunosuppression, causing CMV relapse. Developed CMV colitis. L595S detected day 128 and 156 in plasma and day 190 in colon biopsy. Started on FOS and MBV which resolved CMV. MBV shortage for 3 weeks caused relapse of CMV, but resolved again. MBV continued after 12 months without CMV relapse. Alive.
